actions.action: Pull out the Mother of Thousands/Kalanchoe stowaways and plantlets
Remove the plant from its pot and shake off the old soil
Repot into a pot one size up with drainage holes
Use a richer mix of cactus mix, regular potting soil and perlite
Place in bright light with some direct sun if acclimated
Water when the top inch of soil is dry (check soil)
Trim back leggy stems to encourage fuller shape
If spreading spots, mushy stems, sticky residue or bugs appear, post a sharp close-up

reason: The answer calls the plant mostly healthy and lists low nitrogen in gritty mix and Kalanchoe crowding only as possible mild issues, but its main advice (repot into a less fast-draining, richer mix and remove the stowaways) matches the fix that worked, and nothing it recommends is harmful.
